test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 28 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Cakes are Ice-Creams.

Some Cakes are Butters.

All Cakes are Eggs.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Butters are Ice-creams.

(II) All Eggs are Ice-creams.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is:-

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc324583ff52167bbc57d2938800a8a50df22f7cf0b23aa94ee0b38bb85e808e.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Butters are Ice-creams → **Doesn't follow** (As no direct relationship is given between butter and ice-creams so, it is not definite that some butters are ice-creams.)

(II) All Eggs are Ice-creams → **Doesn't follow **(It is possible but not definite)

Hence, the correct answer is **"Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows".**
